findings.title: Unsanitized Output
findings.body:
`entry.Error` is written raw to the terminal, and the new code only prints it when stderr is a TTY. Parts of that string come from the server: GraphQL error messages appear as-is, e.g. `GraphQL: <message>`.

A malicious or compromised GitHub Enterprise host could return a message containing ANSI/OSC escape sequences. Those sequences would be interpreted by the user's terminal.

HTTP bodies are `%q`-quoted in the tested paths, but GraphQL messages are not. Consider stripping control characters before printing.

findings.title: Security concerns
findings.body: Terminal escape injection: server-controlled error text (e.g. GraphQL error messages from a GHE host) is now printed verbatim to an interactive terminal via `entry.Error`. A malicious host could embed control/escape sequences that manipulate the user's terminal. Uncertain: this depends on whether all error paths escape the server content. Only the HTTP-body path visibly uses quoting.
